newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe to meet Renault head, says method not right.
newsitem.headline: Juppe to meet Renault head, says method not right.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who believes the method used by carmaker Renault was not the right one, was to meet its head Louis Schweitzer later on Wednesday to discuss its decision to close a plant in Belgium, officials said.

An official at Juppe's office said he would meet Schweitzer and Renault general secretary Michel de Virville at 1630 GMT and ask them to inform him about the method used by the group to decide on the closure of the Vilvoorde assembly plant near Brussels. He would also discuss job cuts planned in France.
Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told reporters after a weekly cabinet meeting that Juppe had said the method used by Renault "was not the right one".
Renault caused outrage in Belgium by announcing plans to close the plant, with a loss of 3,100 jobs.
Renault says the closure in July will streamline production so that fewer models are made in more than one plant.
The row over the plant closure and other planned job cuts has highlighted the dilemna faced by French carmakers as they try to improve competitiveness while under government pressure to save jobs.
In Geneva, a London-based car analyst said the stock market would watch the meeting with Juppe closely as a test of the French government's resolve to back Renault.

"This meeting with Juppe will be very important. Either Juppe backs him or not -- and it will be a bad sign if he didn't. It would mean the government is still interfering and doesn't want to accept tough decisions," he said.
